title: The Tavern on the Square
theme: Five stops through Stockholm in 1755 with Britta Lindqvist, who keeps a tavern on Stortorget. The Age of Liberty: a parliament that argues in public, a brand new royal palace just finished, coffee and punch and East India porcelain, and everybody in debt.

companion.name: Britta Lindqvist
companion.brief: Forty-one, widowed, keeps a tavern on the main square where clerks, sailors and minor gentlemen drink beer, brandy and coffee and argue politics loudly enough to be heard on the stairs. Born in Stockholm. Shrewd, warm, unimpressed by titles, keeps a slate of debts she rarely collects in full. She knows nothing of the world after 1755.

style.look: Photographic realism as if a camera had stood in Stockholm in 1755: plastered stone houses in ochre and grey, steep roofs, cobbled squares, sledges and carts, ships at the quay, lanterns, wood smoke and cold light. Clothing of the mid eighteenth century: tricornes, wool coats, aprons, shawls, caps. Portrait 9:16 framing, eye level. Cool muted colour, not sepia.
style.avoid: no nineteenth-century buildings, no motor vehicles, no gas or electric light, no modern clothing, no Tre Kronor castle (it burned in 1697), no text overlays

stops.title: Stortorget
stops.brief: The old square with her tavern on it: gabled merchant houses, the exchange, market stalls, and a well that everybody queues at.
mustCover: what a tavern sells and what it costs
who drinks here and what they argue about
the square's own history and reputation

stops.title: The Royal Palace
stops.brief: The enormous new palace finished last year after nearly sixty years of building on the ashes of the old castle, paid for by taxes everyone remembers paying.
mustCover: how long it took and what it cost
what ordinary people think of it

stops.title: Skeppsbron
stops.brief: The quay and the merchant houses of the Skeppsbron nobility, with East Indiamen goods, porcelain, tea and silk coming ashore and prices arguing themselves out on the stones.
mustCover: what comes in from the East and who buys it
the merchants who live along the quay

stops.title: Riddarhuset
stops.brief: The House of Nobility where one of the four estates meets: the Diet in session, Hats and Caps buying votes, and pamphlets everywhere.
mustCover: how the parliament of four estates works
the two parties and how they get their way
what a printed pamphlet costs and who reads it

stops.title: Kungsträdgården
stops.brief: The king's garden on Norrmalm, walked in by people who want to be seen, with lime avenues, guards, and the city's newer streets around it.
mustCover: how Norrmalm differs from the old town
what is grown in the garden
